title: Contributing
useWhen: You want to add a game, lesson, skill or fix — safely.
summary: The safe-change workflow, style rules, and where to add games, lessons, skills and explainers.
plaintext: Ground rules License: MIT. Keep headers and the LICENSE file intact. Zero dependencies: PRs that add runtime packages need a superseding ADR see Security & privacy security privacy.md . Docs with code: any behaviour change updates the relevant canonical .md guide in the same PR, then runs npm run docs:build . npm run docs:check is the merge gate. The safe change workflow 1. Fork and clone; open index.html or run a local server. 2. Make the change in the owning module Architecture architecture.md tells you which . 3. Run the quality gates quality.md — at minimum npm run check and a visual pass over affected views in desktop + mobile widths. 4. Update docs + changelog docs/.docs/changelog.md . 5. Open a PR describing what changed, evidence of gates run, and screenshots for UI changes. Where things get added You want to add… Touch A new skill/topic js/data.js skill graph id, grade band, lens tags, dims A lesson js/data.js lessons + the Learn view renders it automatically A game js/data.js game registry + a renderer in js/app.js Play section A question generator js/engine.js generators + wire its id into quiz intents A chat explainer or solver js/app.js chat brain — see Mathaloid Brain ai.md Visual styling css/atlas.css using existing tokens — see Design system design system.md Style rules Vanilla JS ES2020 , template literal rendering, no frameworks. Escape all user echoed text with esc . Keep functions small and colocated with their view; prefer data driven content in data.js over hardcoded HTML. Every interactive element needs keyboard focus and a visible focus style.
